title: This week in India's growth story.
caption:
This week in India's growth story: 35 stories covering history, sectors and mindset.

1. He spent years measuring how the Indian Ocean is warming. The world's largest Earth science society just gave him its top communications honor.
2. Maruti Suzuki just started making its own hydrogen. From solar power the factory used to simply waste.
3. He slept on a railway platform to afford weekend engineering classes. He now runs a district as an IAS officer.
4. September 28, 1929: a voice was born in Indore that would become the soundtrack of a nation.
5. He left IIT Bombay for a physics PhD in America. In 2026, he was elected to a society founded in 1780.
6. He's scored more ODI centuries than anyone in history. On September 27, he broke his own record again.
7. His father emigrated from Punjab to study at this college in 1946. In 2026, his son paid off its entire graduating class's loans.
8. A US chip-equipment giant just committed 10,000 crore rupees to India. For a kind of silicon manufacturing nobody's done here before.
9. His father drove an autorickshaw. His mother worked the fields. At 21, he became one of India's youngest IAS officers.
10. September 29, 1997: India launched its own rocket, carrying its own satellite, for the first time.
11. India just built a chip that runs 300 times faster than the silicon in most electronics. It's smaller than a fingernail.
12. He led a database company for less than a year. Then Mark Zuckerberg created a role for him at Meta - reporting directly to him.
13. His father is from Kerala. His mother is from Ukraine. In July 2026, he launched to the International Space Station.
14. She lost her sight completely right before her board exams. She just became the first blind woman to argue a case before India's Supreme Court.
15. September 30, 1989: India launched a submarine it had never built before - and built it anyway.
16. At 11 years old, she just broke a chess record that stood for over two decades.
17. His village had no electricity until he was seven. He now leads Australia's national academy of science.
18. October 1, 1966: India decided tourism was worth its own government company.
19. India just switched on a reactor that makes more fuel than it burns. It's called a breeder reactor - and it's entirely homegrown.
20. She fuses Indian ragas with jazz. In 2026, that earned her a Grammy nomination.
21. India just rolled out its first privately assembled military aircraft. Built at a Tata-Airbus facility in Gujarat.
22. He grew up in a small Gujarat village. In 2026, a US award named after the father of the Green Revolution went to him.
23. He's been blind since birth. He's also saved lives from drowning, 13 times over.
24. His team built a gene therapy from scratch for one baby. It took six months.
25. October 2, 1904: India's second Prime Minister was born on the same day as Gandhi.
26. He mapped the genetics behind heart disease. In 2026, the American Heart Association gave him its top research honor.
27. India just put a passenger boat on the Ganga that runs on hydrogen. Built entirely in India, for India's own waterways.
28. His wife left him. Villagers thought he was mentally ill. He kept building anyway - and changed how millions of women live.
29. October 3, 1978: a Kolkata doctor achieved the world's second-ever IVF birth - alone, with homemade equipment.
30. She gave a US engineering school $100 million. They renamed it after her family.
31. India built a highway with its own wildlife crossing. And camera traps show the animals are actually using it.
32. An IndiGo co-founder is building a 500-bed hospital inside his old engineering college. He's already put in Rs 400 crore of his own money.
33. She leads Teach For India's US arm. In 2026, a new award named her its first-ever winner.
34. She was born blind. Her grandmother, who raised her, is deaf and mute. There was no one in her world who could describe it to her - so she ran through it instead.
35. October 4, 1977: India's External Affairs Minister became the first person to address the UN General Assembly in Hindi.
